chapter: Early life and New York scene
title: First jazz records: Ellington and Armstrong's Hot Five
summary: Wilber recalls Mood Indigo as a toddler and the puzzling first listen to Armstrong Hot Five reissues around 1940 that made him a musician.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, I think the first jazz recording I heard was Duke Ellington's Mood Indigo, which my mother or father got when it came out, which was around 1930, I guess, so I was about two or three years old, and I remember it from then. But I became interested in jazz mainly through being interested in the popular bands of the late 30s. And I think the first time that I heard New Orleans jazz was when I bought the album of Louis Armstrong Hot 5 reissues that

About 1940, yeah. And I remember my first impression of this music, the Muskrat Ramble and Yes, I'm in the Barrel and all those wonderful things, it made no sense to me whatsoever. I was used to the big band riffs and there was no, the melodies were much too complex for me to understand. But I stuck with it and got to love the music. And I think that was the reason I became a musician, was Louis Armstrong's not fine.
